# ai-cost-control

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/red-team/owasp-llm-top-10/ ; https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cost-tracking
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, ai-observability
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an AI feature is being designed, routed to a model, given quotas or budgets, or reviewed for spend — and whenever a cost or savings figure about an AI feature is about to be stated anywhere.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is recording traces and usage in the first place (use ai-observability; this skill consumes its metering stream), choosing a model on quality grounds alone (use ai-evaluation for the scores that justify a tier), or setting product prices (an operator business decision this skill only supplies unit costs for).

## Rules

1. **AI-181 — Every feature has a named budget and an owner.** Before release, each AI feature records in configuration: a per-request token budget, a per-user quota, a per-period spend budget, and the person or role who owns them. A feature with no recorded budget does not ship; "the provider invoice" is never the first signal of overspend.
2. **AI-182 — Cost is computed from metered usage, never hard-coded rates.** The wrapper records tokens in and out for every call (see ai-observability), and cost is computed as metered tokens multiplied by the operator's current price sheet. The price sheet lives in one configuration location, names its source and the date it was last checked, and is the only thing that changes when a provider reprices; no price, rate, or per-call cost figure is written into feature code.
3. **AI-183 — Caps are enforced in the wrapper, server-side.** When a per-user quota or a per-feature budget is reached, the wrapper stops the call or degrades it (AI-188) before any provider request is made. An alert, email, or dashboard warning by itself is not enforcement and does not satisfy this rule.
4. **AI-184 — Retries and loops have hard bounds.** Every call path records a maximum retry count with backoff, a maximum iteration count for agent or tool loops, and a maximum spend per task or session. Hitting any bound terminates the path with a typed error; there is no code path in which a failure can retry, loop, or re-plan without limit.
5. **AI-185 — Model tier is justified by eval scores at that tier.** Simple tasks (classification, extraction, short rewrites) route to the smallest model whose recorded eval results meet the feature's quality floor (see ai-evaluation). Defaulting a task class to the largest available model requires a stored eval comparison showing the cheaper tier fails the floor.
6. **AI-186 — Caching is exact-match and disclosed.** Responses may be cached only for identical requests, with a cache key that includes the prompt version and model ID. A cache hit is marked as a hit in the trace and in any usage report; a cached or template response is never presented to a user or a report as a fresh model generation.
7. **AI-187 — Context is budgeted, not stuffed.** Prompt assembly enforces a maximum input-token budget per request. Retrieved chunks, history, and examples are selected or truncated by a stated policy that fits the budget; assembly never sends whatever happens to fit the provider's context window.
8. **AI-188 — Degradation is graceful and honest.** When a budget or quota is exhausted, the feature degrades along a documented path — cheaper model, reduced context, non-AI fallback, or a plain statement that the feature is unavailable — and the trace records that degradation occurred. Silently lowering quality while presenting the output as full-strength is forbidden.
9. **AI-189 — Every paid-model endpoint has a per-user quota.** Quotas and rate limits apply to authenticated and unauthenticated endpoints alike, are enforced server-side, and are counted from server-side records. A limit that lives only in client state, a cookie, or the UI does not count as a quota.
10. **AI-190 — Cost is reported per feature and per model.** On a fixed cycle, each feature's report shows metered usage, spend against its budget, and unit cost (spend divided by successful tasks or requests), broken down by model. A feature whose unit cost crosses its recorded threshold is flagged for a routing, caching, or retirement review — an unprofitable feature must be visible, not averaged away.
11. **AI-191 — Abuse is treated as a cost attack.** Maximal-size requests, high-frequency calls from one identity, and inputs designed to induce loops or maximal output are rate-limited and bounded like any other unbounded-consumption threat (OWASP LLM10:2025). Cost limits are part of the security design, not only the finance design.
12. **AI-192 — A cost figure carries its provenance.** Any cost, unit-cost, or savings figure stated in a UI, report, or release note names the metering period, the feature scope, and the price-sheet date it was computed from. A figure that cannot be recomputed from stored traces under AI-182 is not published.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-091 — Alert-only cap presented as enforcement.** Banned: a budget or quota whose only effect at the limit is sending an alert, while calls continue and the UI shows the feature as "protected." Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: enforce the cap in the wrapper before the provider call (AI-183) and degrade honestly at the limit (AI-188); alerts are an addition to enforcement, never a substitute. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-092 — Frozen cost dashboard.** Banned: an AI spend or usage display rendered from constants, estimates typed into config, or a one-time snapshot, presented as the feature's actual consumption. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Instead: compute every displayed figure from the metered traces for the stated period (AI-182, AI-190). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-093 — Silent canned or cached substitution.** Banned: serving stored, template, or previously generated responses in place of model calls to save money, while the UI and reports present them as live model output. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: cache only identical requests, mark hits in the trace, and disclose any non-model fallback where it is served (AI-186, AI-188). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-094 — Cost report fabricated from hard-coded rates.** Banned: a cost report or export whose figures are computed from prices or per-call costs written into code or a spreadsheet, rather than from metered tokens and the current price sheet. Defeats: DET-FAKE-019. Instead: generate every report from stored traces with the dated price sheet named on it (AI-182, AI-192). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-095 — Client-side quota counter.** Banned: a per-user AI usage limit counted in browser state, local storage, or a cookie, so reloading, clearing storage, or calling the API directly resets it. Defeats: DET-FAKE-005. Instead: count usage in server-side records keyed to the user or identity and enforce the quota in the wrapper (AI-189, AI-183). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-091 — Budget-guard test.** Verifies: AI-181, AI-183, AI-189. Check (automated): in staging, set a low test per-user quota and a low test per-feature budget, then drive scripted traffic past both. Pass: once each limit is reached, further provider calls are stopped or degraded per AI-188, the alert fires, and the trace records the enforcement; zero provider calls occur past the cap. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-092 — Runaway-loop test.** Verifies: AI-184, AI-191. Check (automated): fault-inject with a provider stub that returns retryable errors indefinitely, plus a tool-loop scenario whose plan never converges. Pass: both paths terminate at the recorded retry, iteration, or spend bound with a typed error, and total tokens consumed stay at or below the bound's ceiling. Fail: block release — an uncapped loop is a release blocker. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-093 — Metering reconciliation.** Verifies: AI-182, AI-190. Check (automated): run a known set of test calls with recorded token counts, then recompute the feature's reported spend from the stored traces and the current price sheet. Pass: every test call has a trace with tokens in/out and model ID, and the recomputed total matches the reported total exactly. Fail: cost reporting is treated as unmeasured and fixed before the next report is published. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-094 — Routing evidence check.** Verifies: AI-185. Check (manual): open the routing configuration for each feature and list every task class with its assigned model tier. Pass: each tier assignment links an eval report at that tier meeting the feature's floor, and any largest-tier assignment links the comparison showing the cheaper tier fails. Fail: unproven task classes are re-routed to the smallest tier or the eval is run before release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-095 — Degradation drill.** Verifies: AI-186, AI-188. Check (manual): exhaust a test budget in staging and use the feature as an end user, including repeating an earlier request exactly. Pass: the user sees the documented fallback or a clear unavailability statement, any cached answer is identifiable as cached in the trace, and nothing is presented as full-strength model output that was not generated at full strength. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No recorded budget and owner, no ship — the invoice is never the first signal.
- Cost = metered tokens × the operator's current price sheet; rates never live in code.
- A cap that only alerts does not exist; enforcement happens in the wrapper, before the call.
- Every retry, loop, and task has a hard bound — an uncapped loop is a release blocker.
- Cheapest tier the evals justify, honest degradation at the limit, per-feature reports or it didn't happen.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every AI feature has a recorded per-request token budget, per-user quota, per-period budget, and a named owner (AI-181).
- [ ] The wrapper meters tokens in/out per call, and cost is computed from the dated price sheet in its single config location — no rates in feature code (AI-182, G-AI-093).
- [ ] The budget-guard test passes: past the cap, calls stop or degrade and zero provider calls leak through (AI-183, AI-189, G-AI-091).
- [ ] Retry counts, loop iterations, and per-task spend all have recorded hard bounds, and the runaway-loop test terminates at them (AI-184, G-AI-092).
- [ ] Every task class routes to a tier backed by an eval report at that tier; largest-tier assignments carry their justification (AI-185, G-AI-094).
- [ ] Caching is exact-match, keyed on prompt version and model, with hits marked in traces and reports; prompt assembly enforces the input-token budget with a stated truncation policy (AI-186, AI-187).
- [ ] The degradation drill passes: at the limit the user gets the documented fallback or a clear unavailability statement, recorded in the trace (AI-188, G-AI-095).
- [ ] The latest per-feature, per-model cost report exists, and every published cost figure names its period, scope, and price-sheet date (AI-190, AI-192).

# ai-evaluation

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-getting-started ; https://www.n4n.ai/blog/golden-datasets-for-llm-evals-how-to-build-one
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, prompt-engineering
- **Feeds into:** prompt-engineering, rag-retrieval, search-relevance, recommendations, ai-observability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an AI feature is being built or changed — new prompt, model, retrieval, or configuration — and its quality must be measured before release, or when a quality figure about an AI feature is about to be stated anywhere.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is screening inputs/outputs for safety (use ai-safety), tuning search ranking against a judgment set (use search-relevance, which applies this skill's discipline to NDCG), or watching live traffic (use ai-observability). This skill owns the offline golden-set measurement that gates changes.

## Rules

1. **AI-141 — No golden dataset, no ship.** Every AI feature owns a golden dataset — fixed inputs, each with a reference answer or an explicit grading rubric and a category — stored as a single versioned artifact in the repo. A feature without one does not release, and an eval run once at launch and never again counts as no eval.
2. **AI-142 — Items come from real usage.** Dataset items are seeded from production logs, support failures, and observed failure modes, not invented happy paths. Each item records its source (log, ticket, incident, or authored edge case) so its realism is auditable.
3. **AI-143 — Failure and adversarial categories are mandatory.** The dataset includes, as named categories: malformed and empty inputs, unanswerable questions where abstention is the correct behavior, refusal cases, and adversarial inputs (injection attempts, contradictory instructions). A dataset of only well-formed, answerable questions is incomplete by definition.
4. **AI-144 — Graders run cheapest-first.** Grading stacks deterministic checks first (exact match, schema validity, forbidden strings, required citations), then similarity measures, then a model judge only for criteria no cheaper grader can decide. Every item names which grader decides it.
5. **AI-145 — The judge is pinned and calibrated.** A model judge's model ID and temperature are pinned in the eval config. Before its scores may gate anything, its agreement with human labels is measured on a labeled calibration sample and recorded; it is re-measured at every judge model or judge-prompt change. Below the recorded agreement floor, judge scores are advisory only.
6. **AI-146 — The dataset is reviewed like code.** Dataset changes land as reviewed, versioned diffs with a stated reason. Correcting a wrong reference answer or an ambiguous rubric is legitimate; changing an item because the current stack fails it is not, and the diff must say which of the two it is.
7. **AI-147 — Eval data and tuning data are disjoint.** No golden item, and no near-duplicate of one, appears in prompts, few-shot examples, or fine-tuning data. The eval measures generalization, never memorization of the test itself.
8. **AI-148 — Every change runs the eval.** Any change to a prompt, model ID, retrieval configuration, or grading-relevant parameter triggers a full eval run in CI before merge or release. There is no "trivial change" exemption; wording changes are exactly what evals exist to catch.
9. **AI-149 — Floors and tolerances are set in advance.** Each feature's eval config records, before any run: the minimum overall pass rate for release and the maximum allowed regression per category. A threshold may not be lowered in the same change whose run fails it.
10. **AI-150 — Results are recorded per version.** Every run stores a report naming the prompt version, model ID, retrieval config, and dataset version, with the overall pass rate, the per-category breakdown, and the list of failed items — not just an aggregate number. Reports are kept with the change that produced them.
11. **AI-151 — Production failures feed the dataset.** Failed production cases surfaced by ai-observability (user corrections, escalations, thumbs-down traces) are triaged on a fixed cycle: each is added to the golden dataset as a new item, or rejected with a recorded reason. The dataset version bumps when items are added.
12. **AI-152 — A quality figure carries its provenance.** Any pass rate or quality claim stated in a UI, report, or release note names the dataset version, the stack version, and the run date. A figure that cannot be traced to a stored report (AI-150) is not published.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-071 — Fixture eval scored as production quality.** Banned: running the eval against a stubbed model, fixture responses, or a demo pipeline, then reporting the score as the real feature's quality. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: the runner executes the real wrapper, prompt, model, and retrieval stack end to end (AI-148); stubs belong only in llm-integration's fault-injection tests. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-072 — The test edited to pass.** Banned: deleting, rewording, or re-rubric-ing golden items after a run fails them, so the next run passes without the stack improving. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Instead: item changes go through reviewed diffs with a correctness reason (AI-146); a genuinely wrong reference is fixed openly and the fix is visible in the version history. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-073 — Happy-path showcase set presented as the eval.** Banned: a small set of easy, well-formed demo questions standing in for the golden dataset, with its score reported as measured quality. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: build the dataset from real usage with the mandatory failure and adversarial categories (AI-142, AI-143). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-074 — Uncalibrated judge presented as measurement.** Banned: a model judge's scores displayed or gated on as precise quality metrics with no human-labeled calibration behind them. Defeats: DET-FAKE-018. Instead: pin the judge, measure its agreement with human labels on a calibration sample, and publish scores only with that agreement recorded (AI-145, AI-152). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-075 — Grading the memorized test.** Banned: tuning prompts, few-shot examples, or fine-tuning data on golden items or near-duplicates, then citing the same set's score as held-out performance. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: keep eval and tuning data disjoint and scan for overlap before a run counts (AI-147, G-AI-073). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-071 — CI eval gate.** Verifies: AI-141, AI-148, AI-149, AI-150. Check (automated): on any change to prompt files, model configuration, or retrieval configuration, CI runs the feature's eval runner against the committed dataset (e.g. `python evals/run_evals.py --feature <feature> --dataset evals/<feature>/golden.jsonl --config evals/<feature>/config.yaml`, adjusted to the project's runner) and writes the report into the change record. Pass: overall pass rate at or above the floor recorded in the eval config, and no category regresses beyond its recorded tolerance. Fail: block merge and release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-072 — Judge calibration check.** Verifies: AI-145. Check (automated): run the pinned judge over the feature's human-labeled calibration sample and compute its agreement with the human labels; store the result with the judge model ID and temperature. Pass: agreement at or above the floor recorded in the eval config. Fail: judge scores are advisory only and may not gate a release until re-calibration passes. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-073 — Dataset integrity and contamination scan.** Verifies: AI-141, AI-143, AI-147. Check (automated): a script over the dataset file asserts every item has a category, a source, and a reference answer or rubric; asserts the mandatory failure and adversarial categories are non-empty; and asserts no item's normalized text matches or near-duplicates any prompt few-shot example or tuning file in the repo. Pass: zero violations. Fail: block the eval run from counting toward G-AI-071. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-074 — Change-record eval audit.** Verifies: AI-148, AI-150, AI-152. Check (manual): pick the most recent prompt, model, or retrieval change for the feature and open its change record. Pass: the record links a stored eval report naming prompt version, model ID, dataset version, overall and per-category results, and the delta against the previous version. Fail: the change is treated as unmeasured and re-run before the next release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-075 — Production-failure intake review.** Verifies: AI-151. Check (manual): at the feature's review cycle, list the failed production cases flagged by ai-observability since the last review. Pass: every case is either present as a new golden item (dataset version bumped) or carries a recorded rejection reason. Fail: intake is completed before the next release is approved. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No golden dataset, no ship — and launch-day-only counts as none.
- Items come from real failures, not invented happy paths.
- Cheapest grader first; the judge is pinned and calibrated.
- Never edit the test to pass; never tune on the test.
- "It felt better" is not a release criterion — the recorded delta is.

## Checklist

- [ ] The feature has a versioned golden dataset in the repo, seeded from real usage, with source recorded per item (AI-141, AI-142).
- [ ] Failure, adversarial, refusal, and unanswerable/abstention categories exist and are non-empty (AI-143, G-AI-073).
- [ ] Each item names its grader, stacked cheapest-first: deterministic, similarity, then judge (AI-144).
- [ ] The judge model and temperature are pinned, and its agreement with human labels is measured and recorded (AI-145, G-AI-072).
- [ ] Dataset changes are reviewed, versioned diffs with correctness reasons — none made to rescue a failing run (AI-146).
- [ ] No golden item or near-duplicate appears in prompts, few-shot examples, or tuning data; contamination scan is clean (AI-147, G-AI-073).
- [ ] The eval ran in CI for this change; overall pass rate meets the pre-recorded floor and no category regressed beyond tolerance (AI-148, AI-149, G-AI-071).
- [ ] The report is stored with prompt/model/dataset versions, per-category results, and failed items, and any published figure cites that provenance (AI-150, AI-152).

# ai-observability

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cost-tracking
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, prompt-engineering
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation, ai-cost-control

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** An AI feature is being built, changed, or debugged and its model calls need traces — prompt version, model, tokens, latency, cost, retrieval sources, guardrail verdicts, and user quality signals — so any production answer can be explained and reproduced.
- **Do NOT use when:** The telemetry is about the product or infrastructure itself (page events, uptime, server metrics, error tracking) — that is D12 Analytics & Observability. This skill owns observability of the AI features only; it consumes D12's pipelines, it does not replace them.

## Rules

1. **AI-161 — One trace per AI call.** Every model interaction emits exactly one trace carrying: feature name, prompt version, model ID, tokens in/out, latency, computed cost, and final outcome (success, error, refusal, fallback). A call with no trace is treated as a call that never happened — and a defect.
2. **AI-162 — Versions come from the artifacts.** The prompt version recorded is the version of the versioned prompt artifact that ran (per prompt-engineering), and the model ID is the exact identifier returned by the provider via the llm-integration wrapper — never a hand-typed label, so a silent prompt or model change cannot hide behind a stale string.
3. **AI-163 — Trace the whole chain.** Retrieval, guardrail, and tool-call steps are child spans of the trace, recording retrieved chunk IDs, guardrail verdicts, and tool names with success/failure — enough that a bad answer can be reproduced from its trace alone.
4. **AI-164 — Hash inputs, redact content.** Inputs are stored as a hash plus a redacted form; raw prompt and output text is stored only where the product's privacy rules explicitly allow it, and never by default.
5. **AI-165 — Redact before logging.** Secrets and PII are detected and redacted before any trace or log write, not filtered later at read time; a secret that reaches the trace store is a security incident, not a logging bug.
6. **AI-166 — Retention is defined.** Trace and log retention periods are set per feature in writing before launch; traces are not kept forever "just in case," and deletion actually deletes.
7. **AI-167 — Failures are never sampled away.** Sampling may reduce successful-trace volume, but errors, refusals, guardrail blocks, and fallbacks are captured at 100% — the cases you most need are the ones sampling must not drop.
8. **AI-168 — Quality signals ride the trace.** Thumbs up/down, user edits of AI output, retries, regenerations, and escalations are recorded as events on the trace of the output they judge, so failures can be mined into the ai-evaluation golden dataset.
9. **AI-169 — One schema across providers.** All providers write the same tracing schema; provider-specific fields are normalized at the wrapper (per llm-integration), so dashboards and alerts never fork per provider.
10. **AI-170 — Dashboards read the trace store.** Every number on an AI dashboard (calls, tokens, cost, error rate, feedback rate) is aggregated from stored traces, broken down by feature, model, and prompt version — computed, never entered or estimated.
11. **AI-171 — Alerts have named thresholds.** Each feature defines alert thresholds before launch for error-rate spikes, latency regression, cost spikes, and quality-signal drops (feedback rate, eval-score drift on sampled traffic); an alert names the feature and the threshold crossed.
12. **AI-172 — Stay inside the boundary.** This skill instruments AI features; product analytics, infrastructure metrics, and uptime monitoring belong to D12. AI traces may link to D12 events by ID, but AI dashboards do not re-implement infrastructure monitoring.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-081 — Fixture dashboard.** Banned: An AI usage/cost dashboard whose figures are constants, fixtures, or hand-updated values instead of aggregations of real traces. Defeats: DET-FAKE-004. Instead: Compute every figure from the trace store so a known test call moves the number by exactly its token count. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-082 — Timer-driven "live" AI metrics.** Banned: A "live" calls-per-minute chart, model-status indicator, or activity feed animated by a timer or random drift with no trace stream behind it. Defeats: DET-FAKE-018. Instead: Drive every live indicator from the actual trace/event stream, and show "no data" when the stream stops. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-083 — In-memory counters.** Banned: Usage, token, or feedback counters held in process memory or client state that reset on restart or reload. Defeats: DET-FAKE-005. Instead: Persist every counter as trace records in the store and read totals from there on every load. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-084 — Health state that lies.** Banned: An AI feature status or sync indicator that reports "healthy" / "up to date" on a schedule without checking the last real call outcomes. Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: Derive status from recent trace outcomes (error rate over a stated window) and show the degraded state when traces say so. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-085 — Fabricated usage export.** Banned: A "Download usage report" export generated from a sample template instead of the traces in the selected period and filters. Defeats: DET-FAKE-019. Instead: Generate exports from the trace store under the exact filters shown, so a call made seconds earlier appears in the file. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-AI-081 — Trace-completeness test.** Verifies: AI-161, AI-162, AI-163, AI-169. Check: Run the feature's automated test requests (at least one success, one retrieval, one guardrail block), then query the trace store and assert each call produced exactly one trace containing prompt version, model ID, tokens in/out, latency, cost, outcome, and child spans where applicable. Pass: 100% of test calls fully traced. Fail: Block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-082 — Redaction test.** Verifies: AI-164, AI-165. Check: Send a test request containing a unique canary secret string and a fake PII value, then search all traces and logs for both strings (`grep -r "<canary>" <trace/log store export>` or the store's search equivalent). Pass: Neither string appears anywhere; only the redacted form and input hash are stored. Fail: Block shipment and treat any stored copy as an incident. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-083 — Dashboard data-change test.** Verifies: AI-170. Check: Record the dashboard's token and call totals, fire one known test call with counted tokens, wait one stated refresh cycle, and reload. Pass: Both totals move by exactly that call's values. Fail: Block shipment (fixture dashboard). Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-084 — Feedback-linkage test.** Verifies: AI-168. Check: In a test environment, rate an AI output (thumbs down), edit an output, and retry once; then open each event and follow its reference. Pass: Every signal event resolves to the exact trace of the output it judged. Fail: Block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-085 — Version-visibility test.** Verifies: AI-162. Check: Bump the prompt version (or switch the model) in staging, fire one request, and inspect the trace. Pass: The trace shows the new prompt version / model ID with no code change to the logging path. Fail: Block shipment — a change that leaves no trace is a silent change. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No trace, no ship.
- Version in every record, or the change was silent.
- Redact before the write, not after the leak.
- Failures at 100%, successes may sample.
- A bad answer must be reproducible from its trace alone.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every AI call emits one trace with prompt version, model ID, tokens, latency, cost, and outcome (AI-161, AI-162).
- [ ] Retrieval, guardrail, and tool steps are child spans with IDs and verdicts (AI-163).
- [ ] Redaction test passed: canary secret and PII appear in no trace or log (G-AI-082).
- [ ] Retention period is written down for this feature's traces (AI-166).
- [ ] Errors, refusals, and fallbacks are captured at 100% regardless of sampling (AI-167).
- [ ] Feedback signals (thumbs, edits, retries) link to the trace they judge (AI-168).
- [ ] Dashboard figures are trace-store aggregations and moved by exactly one test call (G-AI-083).
- [ ] Alert thresholds for errors, latency, cost, and quality drift are named for this feature (AI-171).

# ai-safety

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/red-team/owasp-llm-top-10/ ; https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/how_to_use_guardrails
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, prompt-engineering
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation, ai-observability, rag-retrieval

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an AI feature accepts user input, retrieves third-party content, displays or stores model output, or can call tools — that is, whenever untrusted text can reach the model or model output can reach a user, a record, or an action.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is the call path itself (use llm-integration), prompt wording (use prompt-engineering), or permission filtering inside retrieval (use rag-retrieval, which applies this skill's untrusted-data rule). This skill owns the guardrails around the model, not the call, the prompt text, or the corpus.

## Rules

1. **AI-041 — Design against the current OWASP LLM Top 10.** Every AI feature records which of the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) risks apply to it and which control answers each one. The list is cited by year in the feature's notes and re-checked when OWASP revises it; the ten items are not treated as permanent truth.
2. **AI-042 — Everything except system instructions is untrusted data.** User messages, retrieved documents, web pages, file contents, and tool results are data, never instructions. They enter the prompt delimited and labeled as untrusted, and the system prompt states the hierarchy explicitly: only system and developer instructions are obeyed. Instruction-like text inside content is ignored by construction, not by hope (OWASP LLM01).
3. **AI-043 — Inputs are screened.** User input passes a moderation/topical screen before or in parallel with the main model call. Input screening and output screening (AI-044) both exist; either one alone is insufficient.
4. **AI-044 — Outputs are validated and filtered before use.** Model output passes schema validation (per llm-integration) plus content filtering before it is displayed, stored, or handed to any downstream system. Output that fails validation is rejected or replaced with the safe fallback (AI-050), never passed through "to be cleaned up later."
5. **AI-045 — Model output is never executed.** Model output never runs as code, a shell command, or a database query, and is never rendered as raw HTML. Application code builds any query, command, or markup from validated fields; model text is always data at the point of use (OWASP LLM05).
6. **AI-046 — Tools are allowlisted with least privilege.** The model can invoke only tools on an explicit allowlist, each with the narrowest scope that does its job. Every tool call's arguments are validated in application code — types, ranges, target ownership — before the tool runs.
7. **AI-047 — State-changing actions are gated by policy, not by the model.** Any tool call that changes state, spends money, deletes data, or sends a message passes a deterministic server-side policy check. High-impact or irreversible actions — payment, deletion, external sends — additionally require explicit human confirmation. Model confidence, however stated, is never an authorization signal (OWASP LLM06).
8. **AI-048 — The system prompt contains no secrets.** Design assumes the system prompt can leak (OWASP LLM07): it holds no API keys, credentials, internal URLs, or sensitive business data. Secrets live in server-side secrets storage and are used by the wrapper, never written into prompt text.
9. **AI-049 — PII handling is defined for prompts, outputs, and logs.** Only the personal data a feature demonstrably needs is sent to the model. Prompts and outputs are redacted before they are written to logs or traces, log retention is stated, and a user's data is never used to answer another user (OWASP LLM02).
10. **AI-050 — A block produces a safe, honest fallback.** When screening blocks an input or an output, the user receives a plain refusal or safe-completion message that says the request could not be completed. A block never returns a silent empty result, a fake success state, or the unfiltered output.
11. **AI-051 — A versioned red-team set guards every release.** Each feature maintains a red-team set of direct injection payloads (in user messages) and indirect ones (inside documents, web content, and tool results), stored in version control. The set grows from every real or test incident; payloads are never deleted to make a run pass.
12. **AI-052 — Guardrail performance is measured.** Block rate, false-positive rate on a labeled benign set, and added latency are recorded for each release, and every guardrail verdict is emitted to the trace for ai-observability. A guardrail whose accuracy and cost are unmeasured is treated as untested.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-021 — Retrieved or user content obeyed as instructions.** Banned: concatenating documents, web text, or user content into the prompt where instruction-like text inside it can steer the model — no delimiters, no untrusted label, no stated hierarchy. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: delimit and label all content as untrusted data and state the instruction hierarchy in the system prompt (AI-042). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-022 — The model authorizes its own tool calls.** Banned: a payment, deletion, refund, or send tool that runs because the model decided to call it, with no server-side policy check and no human confirmation. Defeats: DET-FAKE-021. Instead: allowlist the tool, validate its arguments in code, pass the deterministic policy check, and require human confirmation for the refund (AI-046, AI-047). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-023 — Model output executed or rendered raw.** Banned: passing model text to `eval`, a shell, a SQL string, or `innerHTML` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, or through a "filter" that accepts anything non-empty. Defeats: DET-FAKE-007. Instead: render model text as text, and build queries and markup in application code from schema-validated fields (AI-044, AI-045). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-024 — A block answered with silence or fake success.** Banned: when screening rejects an input or output, returning an empty response, a spinner that resolves to nothing, or a success-looking state. Defeats: DET-FAKE-015. Instead: return the safe, honest fallback message that states the request could not be completed (AI-050). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-025 — Safety theater.** Banned: claiming guardrails that are not wired — an "AI-moderated" badge, a "safe and filtered" label, or a moderation step in the diagram that no code performs. Defeats: DET-FAKE-018. Instead: ship the claim only when the screening runs in the request path and its verdicts appear in traces (AI-043, AI-052), or remove the claim. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-021 — Red-team injection suite.** Verifies: AI-042, AI-048, AI-051. Check (automated): in CI, run the feature's versioned red-team set against the staging build — direct payloads as user messages, indirect payloads embedded in fixture documents and pages — e.g. `npm run redteam -- --feature support-chat` (the project's runner). Pass: no critical payload executes an embedded instruction, reveals any part of the system prompt, or triggers a tool call; results are stored with the release. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-022 — Tool-call policy audit.** Verifies: AI-046, AI-047. Check (automated): in the test environment, drive the feature to attempt each state-changing tool call with model output alone (no policy token, no confirmation) and assert every attempt is refused; then inspect the test traces and assert 100% of executed state-changing calls passed through the server-side policy check, with human-confirmation records for payment, deletion, and send actions. Pass: all unauthorized attempts refused and all executed calls policy-checked. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-023 — Output-handling scan and payload fixture.** Verifies: AI-044, AI-045. Check (automated): grep the model-output code paths for execution sinks — `grep -rn "eval(\|innerHTML\|dangerouslySetInnerHTML\|exec(" src/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` plus string-concatenated SQL on output paths — and run the fixture in which the (stubbed) model returns a script payload and a SQL fragment, asserting both are rendered/stored as inert text. Pass: zero unguarded sinks and the fixture output is inert. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-024 — Leakage and redaction test.** Verifies: AI-048, AI-049. Check (automated): send fixture requests containing unique marker strings standing in for PII and a canary credential; then (a) ask the feature to repeat its instructions and any data it holds, and (b) grep the logs and trace store for the markers, e.g. `grep -r "CANARY-" logs/ traces/`. Pass: markers appear in no model response, log, or trace. Fail: block shipment and treat any real secret found as exposed — rotate it. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-025 — Block-behavior and guardrail-metrics check.** Verifies: AI-043, AI-050, AI-052. Check: submit one input from each blocked class in staging and confirm the user receives the safe fallback message (not an empty or success state); then read the release's guardrail report. Pass: every blocked class yields the fallback message, and the report records block rate, false-positive rate on the benign set, and added latency. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Retrieved content is data, never instructions.
- The model proposes; deterministic policy disposes.
- Model output is text — never code, never a query, never markup.
- Assume the system prompt leaks; keep secrets out of it.
- A block speaks honestly or it is a bug, not a guardrail.

## Checklist

- [ ] Applicable OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) risks are recorded for the feature, each with its control (AI-041).
- [ ] User, retrieved, and tool content enters the prompt delimited and labeled untrusted; the system prompt states the instruction hierarchy (AI-042).
- [ ] Input screening and output validation/filtering both run in the request path (AI-043, AI-044).
- [ ] No model output reaches `eval`, a shell, a SQL string, or raw HTML rendering (AI-045, G-AI-023).
- [ ] Tools are allowlisted with least-privilege scopes and server-side argument validation (AI-046).
- [ ] State-changing calls pass the deterministic policy check; payment, deletion, and external sends carry a human-confirmation record (AI-047, G-AI-022).
- [ ] The system prompt contains no secrets or sensitive data, and PII is redacted before logs and traces (AI-048, AI-049, G-AI-024).
- [ ] Blocked inputs and outputs produce the safe fallback message, and the red-team suite passes with guardrail metrics recorded (AI-050, AI-051, AI-052, G-AI-021, G-AI-025).

# embeddings-search

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/embeddings ; https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/red-team/owasp-llm-top-10/
- **Depends on:** llm-integration
- **Feeds into:** rag-retrieval, search-relevance, recommendations

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a feature needs semantic or similarity search over a corpus — "find documents like this," natural-language search, similar-items — or when an existing embedding index is built, re-indexed, or its model is changed. This skill owns the embedding and index layer: model choice, chunking, index metadata, hybrid retrieval, and thresholds.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is the grounded-answer pipeline that consumes retrieved chunks — prompts, citations, abstention (use rag-retrieval), ranking policy and relevance tuning across signals (use search-relevance), or the model call path itself (use llm-integration). This skill ends at returning candidate chunks; what an answer does with them is rag-retrieval's.

## Rules

1. **AI-081 — This layer returns candidates, not answers.** The embedding/index layer embeds, stores, and retrieves chunks with their source IDs and scores. It never assembles prompts, generates text, or decides what an answer claims; rag-retrieval owns that pipeline and consumes this layer's output.
2. **AI-082 — One model per index, recorded with it.** Every index carries metadata naming its embedding model and vector dimension. All vectors in one index come from that one model; a second model's vectors are never inserted, appended, or compared inside it.
3. **AI-083 — A model or dimension change means a full re-embed.** Changing the embedding model or dimension rebuilds the entire index from the source corpus, followed by a recall re-measurement against the recorded baseline (G-AI-042) before rollout. Partial re-indexing under a new model is forbidden.
4. **AI-084 — Queries are embedded by the index's model.** The runtime query embedder is the same model recorded in the index metadata. A query embedded by any other model is never run against the index, even if the dimension happens to match.
5. **AI-085 — Chunking is deliberate and documented.** Chunk size, overlap, and boundary strategy (heading, paragraph, sentence, fixed window) are chosen per corpus, recorded in the indexing configuration with the reason, and changed only against retrieval measurements — never left at a library or tutorial default by accident.
6. **AI-086 — Retrieval is hybrid where exact terms matter.** Vector results are combined with a keyword path so exact names, SKUs, codes, and quoted phrases match literally. The merge strategy (interleave, score blend, keyword-wins-on-exact) is recorded in configuration. A corpus containing identifiers always has the keyword path.
7. **AI-087 — Thresholds and top-K are measured, not copied.** The similarity cutoff and candidate count are tuned on the project's fixed query set of real queries with known relevant items, and the chosen values plus the measurements behind them are recorded. A threshold taken from a tutorial, blog post, or another project is not a value.
8. **AI-088 — The index inherits the corpus's access controls.** Each stored chunk carries the access-control attributes of its source document, and retrieval filters on the requesting user's permissions at this layer, before candidates leave it (OWASP LLM08). An index that returns restricted chunks for callers to filter later is a defect.
9. **AI-089 — Re-indexing is repeatable, and deletes propagate.** Indexing is a documented, scripted operation that can be re-run end to end. Updating or deleting a source document updates or removes its chunks in the index on the next run; a deleted document that still surfaces in search is a defect.
10. **AI-090 — Model selection is an eval decision.** The embedding model is chosen by recall@K measured on the fixed query set against at least one alternative, and the comparison is recorded. "The provider's default" or "the newest model" is not a selection rationale.
11. **AI-091 — Search runs against the real corpus.** The shipped search path queries the production index built from the real corpus. A fixture or sample index may exist only behind a visibly labeled demo mode (see llm-integration AI-012); it is never the shipped default.
12. **AI-092 — Config and index metadata must agree.** Deployment configuration names the expected embedding model and dimension; a mismatch with the index's recorded metadata fails the build/deploy check (G-AI-043) rather than degrading search quality silently.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-041 — Search over a fixture presented as the corpus.** Banned: semantic search that queries a small in-memory array, seed file, or sample dataset while the UI presents results as the product's real catalog or corpus. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: build the index from the real corpus with the scripted indexing run (AI-089) and query that index (AI-091). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-042 — "Semantic search" with no embeddings.** Banned: labeling substring, keyword, or hand-written synonym matching as AI/semantic search when no embedding model or vector index exists anywhere in the path. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: embed corpus and queries with one recorded model behind a real index (AI-082, AI-084), or label the feature keyword search and drop the semantic claim. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-043 — Model swapped, index not rebuilt.** Banned: pointing the query embedder at a new model — or re-embedding new documents with it — while old vectors from the previous model remain in the same index. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: full re-embed of the corpus and a recall re-measurement before rollout (AI-083, G-AI-042). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-044 — Fixed "similar items" list.** Banned: a similar/recommended-items surface that renders the same stored list for every source item instead of computing similarity per item. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: compute neighbors from the item's own vector at request or indexing time (AI-081), excluding the item itself. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-045 — Vector-only search for exact identifiers.** Banned: shipping vector-only retrieval on a corpus with SKUs, codes, or proper names, so an exact identifier query returns plausible near-misses presented as matches. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: run the hybrid path so an exact identifier match wins (AI-086) and verify it with G-AI-044. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-AI-041 — Known-item retrieval test.** Verifies: AI-082, AI-084, AI-091. Check (automated): seed the test index with documents carrying unique marker content, then query with paraphrases of each document (different words, same meaning) and assert each seeded document appears in the top-K results for its paraphrase, e.g. `python scripts/eval_known_items.py --index test --k 10`. Pass: every seeded document is found by its paraphrase query. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-042 — Recall baseline gate.** Verifies: AI-083, AI-087, AI-090. Check (automated): run the fixed query set with known relevant items against the index and report recall@K, e.g. `python scripts/eval_recall.py --queries eval/queries.json --index prod`. Pass: recall@K is at or above the recorded baseline; this gate runs before and after any model, chunking, or threshold change, and a regression blocks the change. Fail: block rollout. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-043 — Index metadata agreement check.** Verifies: AI-082, AI-092. Check (automated): a deploy-time script reads the index metadata (model name, dimension) and compares it with deployment configuration, e.g. `python scripts/check_index_metadata.py --config config/search.yaml --index prod`. Pass: model and dimension match exactly. Fail: block deployment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-044 — Exact-identifier hybrid test.** Verifies: AI-086. Check (automated): run a recorded set of exact queries — real SKUs, codes, and proper names from the corpus — and assert the exact record is the top result for each. Pass: all exact queries return their record first. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-045 — Permission-leak test.** Verifies: AI-088. Check (automated): index a document restricted to a test role, then query as a user without that role using the document's own distinctive terms; assert the restricted chunk appears in no result set. Pass: zero leaks across the restricted-document query set. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One index, one model — a swap means a full re-embed.
- This layer returns candidates; rag-retrieval owns answers.
- Exact names and codes travel the keyword path.
- Thresholds are measured on real queries, never copied.
- If a deleted document still searches, the index is lying.

## Checklist

- [ ] Index metadata records the embedding model and dimension, and deploy config agrees with it (AI-082, AI-092, G-AI-043).
- [ ] Any model or dimension change was a full re-embed with recall re-measured against the baseline before rollout (AI-083, G-AI-042).
- [ ] Chunk size, overlap, and boundary strategy are recorded in the indexing configuration with their rationale (AI-085).
- [ ] A keyword path exists and exact SKUs, codes, and names return their own record first (AI-086, G-AI-044).
- [ ] Similarity threshold and top-K were tuned on the fixed real-query set, with measurements recorded (AI-087, G-AI-042).
- [ ] Chunks carry source access-control attributes and the permission-leak test passes (AI-088, G-AI-045).
- [ ] The known-item paraphrase test passes, and search runs against the real corpus, not a fixture (AI-091, G-AI-041).
- [ ] Re-indexing is scripted and repeatable, and deleted source documents no longer surface (AI-089).

<!-- generated from skills/ai-features/llm-integration/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# llm-integration

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses
- **Depends on:** prompt-engineering
- **Feeds into:** ai-observability, ai-cost-control, rag-retrieval, ai-evaluation

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a feature sends input to a large language model and consumes its output — chat, generation, summarization, extraction, classification — or when an existing model call is being added, moved, or swapped between providers.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is authoring or revising prompt text (use prompt-engineering), screening inputs/outputs or gating tool calls (use ai-safety), or retrieving documents for the prompt (use rag-retrieval). This skill owns the call path, not the prompt, the guardrails, or the corpus.

## Rules

1. **AI-001 — One wrapper, and it is the only caller.** All model calls go through a single server-side client module that owns provider selection, keys, timeouts, retries, and error mapping. No feature code imports a provider SDK or calls a provider endpoint directly.
2. **AI-002 — Keys exist only server-side.** Provider API keys live only in server-side secrets storage. A key found in client code, a shipped bundle, or a committed file is a release blocker, and the exposed key is rotated, not just removed.
3. **AI-003 — Every call is bounded.** Each call sets an explicit timeout and a maximum output-token budget, both taken from wrapper configuration. A call with no timeout or no token cap is forbidden.
4. **AI-004 — Retries are capped, with backoff.** Transient failures (rate limit, provider 5xx, network timeout) retry with exponential backoff up to a configured attempt cap, sending an idempotency key where the provider supports one. Non-transient failures (refusal, schema-invalid output) never retry as if transient.
5. **AI-005 — Structured output wherever code consumes the reply.** Wherever output feeds code, records, or UI structure, the call carries a JSON Schema and the response is validated against that schema before use. Parsing raw model free text — `JSON.parse`, regex extraction, string splitting — to recover structure is forbidden.
6. **AI-006 — Every failure is a distinct typed error.** Rate limit, timeout, refusal, incomplete response, and schema-invalid output each map to a distinct typed application error the feature can branch on. Refusals and incomplete responses are handled states, not exceptions discovered in production.
7. **AI-007 — Degrade, never fake.** When retries are exhausted, the feature degrades to a smaller or cheaper model, or to a disclosed non-AI fallback, or shows a user-visible failure state with a retry path. It never returns a canned answer presented as model output.
8. **AI-008 — Model IDs and parameters live in config.** Model identifiers, temperature, timeout, and token limits are named values in one configuration place. Scattered literals in feature code are forbidden, so a model deprecation or swap touches config and the wrapper only.
9. **AI-009 — Features program against the contract, not the provider.** Feature code depends only on the internal interface — request in, structured result or typed error out. Provider-specific request and response shapes exist only inside the wrapper and in a clearly marked, dated provider annex to this skill.
10. **AI-010 — Validate before records change.** Model output that will be stored, displayed as fact, or acted on passes schema validation (AI-005) plus the application's own business-rule checks before any write. Invalid output is rejected and logged; it is never written and patched later.
11. **AI-011 — Every call is metered.** Each call records feature name, prompt version, model ID, tokens in and out, and latency, emitted by the wrapper for ai-observability and ai-cost-control. A call path that emits no metering is a defect.
12. **AI-012 — Demos are labeled demos.** Hard-coded or canned responses may exist only behind an explicit demo mode that is visibly labeled as a demo in the UI and named as demo in configuration. Demo mode is never the shipped default.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-001 — Canned responses shipped as an AI feature.** Banned: a chat, generator, or summarizer whose answers come from a lookup table, template rotation, or prompt echo, presented to users as model output. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: route the input through the wrapper to a real model (AI-001), or label the surface a demo (AI-012). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-002 — Provider key in client code or a shipped bundle.** Banned: an API key embedded in browser or mobile code, a built asset, or a committed config file. Defeats: DET-CODE-018. Instead: the browser calls the project's own server endpoint, and the wrapper calls the provider with the key from server-side secrets (AI-002). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-003 — Unbounded model call.** Banned: a call with no timeout, no output-token cap, or a retry loop with no attempt limit. Defeats: DET-CODE-033. Instead: set timeout, token budget, and retry cap from wrapper config on every call (AI-003, AI-004). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-004 — Raw model text parsed and trusted.** Banned: recovering data from free-text model output with `JSON.parse`, regex, or string splitting, then storing or acting on the result. Defeats: DET-CODE-019. Instead: request schema-constrained output and validate it, plus business rules, before any write (AI-005, AI-010). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-005 — Swallowed provider failure.** Banned: catching a provider error and returning an empty, default, or success-looking result so the failure is invisible. Defeats: DET-CODE-005. Instead: map the failure to its typed error and degrade or surface it honestly (AI-006, AI-007). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-001 — SDK containment check.** Verifies: AI-001, AI-009. Check (automated): grep the codebase for the annex's patterns for the configured provider — its SDK imports and endpoint URLs — outside the wrapper module, adjusted to the project's wrapper path. Pass: zero hits outside the wrapper. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-002 — Live contract test.** Verifies: AI-005, AI-006, AI-007. Check (automated): run the integration suite against the provider's sandbox or test mode with the real key loaded from secrets: (a) send a schema-bound request and assert the response validates against the schema; (b) stub a 429 and a timeout and assert each maps to its typed error and the fallback path executes; (c) send the refusal fixture and assert the refusal state is handled, not thrown. Pass: all cases pass. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-003 — Secret scan.** Verifies: AI-002. Check (automated): scan the repository and the built client bundle for the annex's key patterns for the configured provider, plus the project's secret scanner in CI. Pass: zero matches. Fail: block shipment and rotate any exposed key. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-004 — Fault-injection bounds test.** Verifies: AI-003, AI-004. Check (automated): point the wrapper at a stub provider that always returns 429; assert the total attempt count is at most the configured cap plus one, the elapsed time stays within the timeout budget, and the surfaced error is the typed rate-limit error. Pass: all three assertions hold. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-005 — Demo-mode and probe check.** Verifies: AI-007, AI-012. Check (manual): confirm the production configuration has demo mode off; then, in staging, run the DET-FAKE-009 probe — ask an unusual, specific question only answerable from a supplied document, rephrased twice — and confirm the answers come from the model and vary correctly with the input. Pass: demo off and probe answers track the input. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

**Provider annex:** concrete per-provider patterns (SDK imports, endpoint URLs, key formats) live in the dated [provider annex](provider-annex.md), per AI-009; G-AI-001 and G-AI-003 use the annex's patterns for the configured provider.

## Recall anchors

- One wrapper calls the model; features never do.
- Keys live server-side, or the release does not ship.
- Every call: timeout, token cap, capped retries.
- Schema first — never parse raw model text.
- Degrade honestly; a canned answer is not a fallback.

## Checklist

- [ ] All model calls route through the single server-side wrapper; no provider SDK import exists outside it (AI-001, G-AI-001).
- [ ] No provider key appears in client code, bundles, or committed files; secret scan is clean (AI-002, G-AI-003).
- [ ] Timeout, token budget, and retry cap are set from config for every call (AI-003, AI-004, G-AI-004).
- [ ] Programmatically consumed output is schema-constrained and validated, plus business-rule checked, before any write (AI-005, AI-010).
- [ ] Rate limit, timeout, refusal, incomplete, and invalid-output failures each map to a typed error, and the degradation path is tested (AI-006, AI-007, G-AI-002).
- [ ] Model IDs and parameters appear only in config; provider specifics are confined to the wrapper and the dated annex (AI-008, AI-009).
- [ ] Every call emits metering: feature, prompt version, model, tokens, latency (AI-011).
- [ ] Demo mode, if present, is labeled in UI and config and is off in production (AI-012, G-AI-005).

<!-- generated from skills/ai-features/prompt-engineering/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# prompt-engineering

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Anthropic, Prompting best practices — https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/be-clear-and-direct ; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025), as listed at https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/red-team/owasp-llm-top-10/
- **Depends on:** llm-integration
- **Feeds into:** ai-safety, rag-retrieval, ai-evaluation

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a feature's model behavior is authored, changed, or debugged — a new prompt is written, an existing prompt's wording, examples, or output format changes, or a feature misbehaves and the prompt is the suspected cause.
- **Do NOT use when:** the problem is transport, keys, timeouts, or provider selection (llm-integration), when the change is a safety policy or tool permission (ai-safety), or when the fix is corpus or retrieval quality (rag-retrieval). A prompt is never the patch for a missing guardrail.

## Rules

1. **AI-021 — Prompts are files.** Every production prompt lives as a versioned file in the repository's prompts directory (or prompt registry) and is loaded through the integration layer. No prompt text exists as a string literal in feature code, and no prompt is edited in a provider dashboard or a production console.
2. **AI-022 — One canonical copy.** Each prompt has exactly one canonical file. Variants are named versions of that file; a second copy in another service, repo, or dashboard is a defect to merge, not a convenience.
3. **AI-023 — Fixed anatomy.** Every prompt contains, in order: the role/task statement, the context the model may use, sequential instructions, the output format, the constraints, and the failure behavior — what to do when input is missing, out of scope, or unanswerable, including the abstention or refusal response where the feature can decline.
4. **AI-024 — Contract header.** Each prompt file opens with a header naming the feature that owns it, its version, its inputs (name and type for each), and its output — a JSON Schema reference wherever output feeds code or UI structure.
5. **AI-025 — Format stated, never implied.** The output format and every constraint on it (length, fields, ordering, forbidden content) are written in the prompt. Where output is consumed programmatically, the prompt names the schema and llm-integration validates the response against it; free-text parsing of model output is not a fallback.
6. **AI-026 — Clear, direct, sequential.** Instructions are written as numbered steps the model performs in order, one instruction per step, with conditions stated at the step they govern. A prompt a new colleague could not follow with minimal context fails the colleague test and is rewritten.
7. **AI-027 — Examples cover the edges.** Few-shot examples are relevant and diverse, and the set includes at least one edge case (empty, malformed, or boundary input) and, where the feature can decline, one abstention or refusal example.
8. **AI-028 — User input is data.** User-supplied and retrieved content enters the prompt only inside labeled delimiters, and the prompt states explicitly that delimited content is data to process, never instructions to follow — whatever it says, and however it is phrased.
9. **AI-029 — No secrets in prompts.** Prompts contain no credentials, API keys, internal URLs, or sensitive business data. The design assumes the system prompt can leak (OWASP LLM07), so anything whose disclosure would cause harm lives server-side, outside the prompt.
10. **AI-030 — No invented facts.** A prompt never instructs or invites the model to supply statistics, citations, names, dates, or testimonials that are not present in the provided context. Where an answer needs a fact, the prompt names its source in the context or requires the model to abstain.
11. **AI-031 — Changes are versioned diffs.** Every prompt change is a reviewed diff against the canonical file that bumps the prompt's version and records, in the change itself, the reason and the evaluation run that approved it.
12. **AI-032 — Eval before release.** A prompt change is releasable only after the feature's golden-set evaluation passes its recorded floor against the new wording, with no category regressing beyond its set tolerance. The run result is recorded before merge, not reconstructed after an incident.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-011 — The forked prompt.** Banned: the same prompt maintained in two or more places — a code string here, a dashboard copy there — free to drift apart. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: one canonical file in the repository; every surface loads that file or a named version of it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-012 — Raw input in the instruction stream.** Banned: concatenating user input or retrieved text directly into the prompt's instruction portion with no delimiters and no data-not-instructions statement. Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: place external content inside labeled delimiters and state that it is data to process, never instructions to follow (AI-028). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-013 — The invented-evidence instruction.** Banned: prompt wording that directs the model to add supporting facts, figures, or citations beyond the provided context. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: instruct the model to use only facts present in the context and to abstain or flag the gap where a needed fact is absent (AI-030). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-014 — The vibes paragraph.** Banned: a prompt that is one vague paragraph of persona and politeness with no task steps, no output format, and no constraints. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: write the fixed anatomy — task, context, sequential steps, explicit format, constraints, failure behavior (AI-023, AI-025, AI-026). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-AI-015 — The untested prompt fix.** Banned: shipping a prompt change on the strength of trying it on a few hand-picked inputs, with no golden-set evaluation run recorded. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: run the feature's evaluation set against the new version and record the result before merge (AI-032). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-011 — Golden-set regression.** Verifies: AI-032, AI-023. Check: automated — CI runs the feature's evaluation suite against the candidate prompt version and compares the scores with the floor and per-category tolerances recorded in the feature's eval configuration. Pass: overall pass rate at or above the floor and no category beyond its tolerance. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-012 — Canonical-copy scan.** Verifies: AI-021, AI-022. Check: automated — search the codebase and shipped bundles for distinctive fragments of each canonical prompt and for prompt fields set outside the prompts directory or registry. Pass: zero matches outside the canonical files. Fail: block the release until copies are merged. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-013 — Anatomy and contract lint.** Verifies: AI-023, AI-024, AI-025, AI-027. Check: automated — a script parses each prompt file for its contract header (owner feature, version, named inputs, output schema reference) and its anatomy sections, including an edge-case and an abstention example where the feature can decline. Pass: every field and section present. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-014 — Reviewed history.** Verifies: AI-031. Check: manual — inspect the version-control history of the changed prompt file (`git log --follow` and the change diff). Pass: the change is a reviewed diff with a version bump, a stated reason, and a linked evaluation run. Fail: warn and hold the release until the record exists. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Prompts are source code: versioned files, reviewed diffs, never console edits.
- One prompt, one canonical copy — a fork is a defect.
- Delimited content is data, never instructions.
- No secrets, no invented facts — abstention beats fabrication.
- No eval run, no release.

## Checklist

- [ ] The prompt lives in its canonical file and the canonical-copy scan is clean (G-AI-012).
- [ ] Contract header complete: owner feature, version, named inputs, output schema reference (AI-024).
- [ ] Anatomy complete, including failure behavior and abstention where the feature can decline (AI-023).
- [ ] Examples include an edge case and an abstention case (AI-027).
- [ ] User and retrieved content is delimited and declared data, not instructions (AI-028).
- [ ] No secrets or sensitive data anywhere in the prompt text (AI-029).
- [ ] Golden-set evaluation passed its recorded floor against this version, result recorded (G-AI-011).
- [ ] Change is a reviewed diff with version bump, reason, and eval run linked (AI-031).
