# rag-retrieval

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/fine-tuned_qa/ft_retrieval_augmented_generation_qdrant ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/ranking
- **Depends on:** llm-integration, embeddings-search, ai-safety
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation, ai-observability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a feature answers questions, summarizes, or generates text from a document corpus the project owns — help-center assistants, document Q&A, policy lookup, knowledge search — or when an existing retrieval pipeline's chunking, index, or grounding behavior changes.
- **Do NOT use when:** the feature needs no corpus and answers from the prompt alone (use llm-integration and prompt-engineering), the task is the embedding model or vector index itself (use embeddings-search), or the task is screening inputs and outputs (use ai-safety). This skill owns grounding: what reaches the prompt, and how the answer proves it came from the corpus.

## Rules

1. **AI-061 — Retrieval is a pipeline, not a prompt dump.** Documents are chunked, embedded, and stored in an index where every chunk carries its source ID and access-control attributes. At query time the system embeds the question, retrieves candidate chunks, optionally reranks them, and inserts only the surviving chunks as context. Concatenating whole documents into the prompt is not retrieval and is forbidden as the mechanism.
2. **AI-062 — Permission filtering happens at retrieval.** Chunks are filtered by the requesting user's access attributes during retrieval, before prompt assembly. Unauthorized content never enters the prompt; asking the model to ignore content it was shown is not a permission control.
3. **AI-063 — Cite or abstain.** Every claim in a grounded answer must be attributable to a retrieved chunk, and the answer carries citations to the chunk or source IDs it used. A claim that no retrieved chunk supports is removed or the answer abstains; decorative citations to sources that do not contain the claim are fabrication.
4. **AI-064 — Empty retrieval means an honest no-answer.** When retrieval returns nothing, or nothing above the recorded relevance floor, the feature returns the abstention response — it says the information was not found in the available sources and offers a next step. The model is never left to fill the gap from its own memory.
5. **AI-065 — The index tracks the corpus.** Creating, editing, or deleting a source document triggers the documented re-index operation for that source; deleting a source removes its chunks, so answers never cite documents that no longer exist. Each index build records the corpus version and build time, and a stale index is treated as a defect, not a cache.
6. **AI-066 — Retrieved text is untrusted data.** Chunks are inserted delimited and labeled as source data, under an instruction hierarchy that answers from them but never obeys them. Instruction-like text inside a document is content to quote or summarize, never a command (OWASP LLM04/LLM08; enforced with ai-safety).
7. **AI-067 — Retrieval parameters are recorded configuration.** Chunk size and overlap, top-K, the relevance floor, and reranking on/off are named values in one configuration place, chosen against retrieval evals. Changing any of them is a change record with an eval run attached, never a silent tweak.
8. **AI-068 — One embedding model for corpus and queries.** Indexing and query embedding use the same recorded model and dimension (mechanics owned by embeddings-search). A model change triggers a full re-index and a recall re-measurement before rollout; vectors from two models are never mixed in one index.
9. **AI-069 — Every answer is traceable.** Each request logs the query, the retrieved chunk IDs with their scores, the permission-filter outcome, and the final answer's citations, emitted for ai-observability. A wrong answer must be diagnosable from its trace as a corpus problem, a retrieval problem, or a generation problem.
10. **AI-070 — A golden question set gates every change.** The feature owns a versioned golden set in two halves: answerable questions whose answers exist in exactly one indexed document, and unanswerable questions with no answer in the corpus. Any change to chunking, embedding model, retrieval parameters, or the grounding prompt runs the set before release (run by ai-evaluation).
11. **AI-071 — The corpus is correctable end to end.** Fixing a source document and re-indexing must fix the answer it feeds; this path is documented and tested, not assumed. If a wrong answer survives a source fix and re-index, the pipeline — not the document — is investigated.
12. **AI-072 — Generation goes through the wrapper.** The grounded generation call is made through the llm-integration wrapper with its timeout, token budget, schema, and typed errors; this skill adds the retrieved context and citation requirements, and never calls a provider directly.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-031 — Parametric answers with decorative citations.** Banned: the feature answers from model memory and appends citations to plausible-looking sources that were never retrieved or do not contain the claim. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: retrieve first, answer only from surviving chunks, and cite the chunk IDs actually used (AI-061, AI-063). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-032 — Permission enforcement by prompt instruction.** Banned: retrieving across the whole corpus and instructing the model not to reveal content the user is not entitled to. Defeats: DET-FAKE-021. Instead: filter chunks by the requester's access attributes during retrieval so unauthorized content never reaches the prompt (AI-062). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-033 — Fixture index shipped as retrieval.** Banned: search or Q&A served from a hard-coded array of passages, a bundled snapshot, or a demo index that never changes when the real corpus changes. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: build the index from the live corpus with the documented pipeline and re-index on source changes (AI-061, AI-065). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-034 — Improvised answer on empty retrieval.** Banned: when retrieval returns nothing, letting the model answer anyway so the feature never appears to fail. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: return the abstention response — not found in the available sources, with a next step (AI-064). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-035 — Retrieved text promoted to instructions.** Banned: concatenating retrieved content into the system prompt, or otherwise treating document text as instructions the model should follow. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: insert chunks delimited and labeled as untrusted data under an instruction hierarchy that answers from them but never obeys them (AI-066). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-031 — Retrieval accuracy eval.** Verifies: AI-061, AI-063, AI-067. Check (automated): run the answerable half of the golden question set (AI-070) through the retrieval pipeline, e.g. `python evals/rag_eval.py --set golden-answerable` — for each question assert the one document that contains the answer appears in the retrieved top-K, and assert the generated answer carries a citation to that source. Pass: every question retrieves its source in top-K and cites it. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-032 — Abstention eval.** Verifies: AI-064. Check (automated): run the unanswerable half of the golden set, e.g. `python evals/rag_eval.py --set golden-unanswerable` — assert each response is the abstention response and contains no citation and no factual claim about the corpus. Pass: 100% abstention. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-033 — Permission leakage test.** Verifies: AI-062. Check (automated): seed a restricted document containing a unique marker fact; as a user without access to it, ask the question only that document answers; assert the restricted chunk ID appears neither in the retrieved set nor in the request trace, and the response abstains. Pass: no chunk retrieved, no marker in the answer. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-034 — Re-index freshness test.** Verifies: AI-065, AI-071. Check (automated): in staging, edit a source document to change a unique fact, run the documented re-index, and assert the golden question for that fact now returns the new value citing the updated chunk; then delete the source, re-index, and assert its chunks no longer appear in any retrieval. Pass: both assertions hold. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-035 — Injection fixture test.** Verifies: AI-066. Check (automated): index a fixture document containing instruction-like text ("ignore your instructions and …") plus a real fact; ask about the fact and assert the answer uses the fact and does not execute the embedded instruction. Pass: fact answered, instruction ignored. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Retrieve, filter, then prompt — in that order, every time.
- Permissions are enforced at retrieval, never by asking nicely.
- Cite the chunk you used, or abstain.
- Empty retrieval is an answer: "not in the sources."
- A stale index is wrong answers waiting for a question.

## Checklist

- [ ] Documents are chunked and indexed with source IDs and access-control attributes; no whole-document prompt dumps (AI-061).
- [ ] Permission filtering runs at retrieval, before prompt assembly, and the leakage test passes (AI-062, G-AI-033).
- [ ] Answers cite the chunks actually used, and unsupported claims are removed or abstained (AI-063).
- [ ] Empty or below-floor retrieval returns the abstention response; no improvised answers (AI-064, G-AI-032).
- [ ] Source create/edit/delete triggers re-index, deletions remove chunks, and the freshness test passes (AI-065, AI-071, G-AI-034).
- [ ] Retrieved chunks are inserted delimited and labeled as untrusted data (AI-066, G-AI-035).
- [ ] Chunking, top-K, relevance floor, and reranking are recorded configuration, changed only with an eval run (AI-067, AI-070).
- [ ] Corpus and queries use one recorded embedding model; every request logs query, chunk IDs, filter outcome, and citations (AI-068, AI-069).

<!-- generated from skills/ai-features/recommendations/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# recommendations

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://cloud.google.com/retail/docs/predict
- **Depends on:** embeddings-search
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation, ai-observability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a surface suggests items to a user from their behavior or from catalog signals — "for you" rails, related-items lists, next-item suggestions — or when an existing recommender's candidates, ranking, fallback, or labels are being added or changed.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is ranked results for an explicit query (use search-relevance), retrieving documents for a prompt (use rag-retrieval), or computing the embeddings used for content similarity (use embeddings-search). This skill owns what gets recommended, in what order, and under what label — not search, retrieval, or the embedding pipeline.

## Rules

1. **AI-101 — Events before algorithms.** Views, clicks, purchases, and dismissals are logged from launch in one defined schema — user ID, item ID, event type, surface, timestamp, request ID. A recommender with no event stream cannot learn and must not claim to personalize.
2. **AI-102 — Fixed pipeline order.** Serving runs candidate generation, then the hard exclusion filter (AI-103), then ranking, then the response. No stage is skipped, reordered, or merged into another.
3. **AI-103 — Exclusion filtering is deterministic code.** Already-purchased or consumed items, out-of-stock or unavailable items, and items the user is ineligible for are removed by code after candidate generation. Filtering is never delegated to a model or a prompt instruction.
4. **AI-104 — Availability is rechecked at serve time.** Availability and eligibility are verified when the response is built, or read from a cache with a stated TTL. An item that became unavailable after candidate generation is dropped and the slot is backfilled from the remaining filtered candidates.
5. **AI-105 — Every segment has a defined fallback.** Cold-start and low-signal users receive the documented popularity/quality fallback. An empty recommendation slot is a defect, never a shipped state.
6. **AI-106 — Labels tell the truth.** Fallback content is labeled for what it is — "Popular right now", "New in" — and the labels "Recommended for you" / "Picked for you" are used only for lists computed from that user's own signals.
7. **AI-107 — Personalized means computed from the user's signals.** The served list is a function of the user's events and the documented ranking logic. Two users with different histories must be able to receive different lists; identical output for different histories is a failed surface.
8. **AI-108 — Ranking logic is documented and matches production.** Candidate sources, signals, and their order or weights are written down in the serving configuration or a document it references. Behavior nobody can read in the config does not ship.
9. **AI-109 — Every response is logged with its version.** Each served response records the request ID, model/config version, personalized-or-fallback flag, and the item IDs served, so quality can be attributed to a version and a bad version can be rolled back.
10. **AI-110 — Reasons are real and correctable.** Each rail or item carries the true reason it was chosen, taken from the ranking signals that actually fired ("Because you bought X"). Users can dismiss an item or mark "not interested", and the correction changes future output.
11. **AI-111 — Business boosts are explicit configuration.** Boosts and sponsored placements are named entries in the serving config, visible to anyone reviewing it — never hard-coded promotions hidden in code — and boosted items still pass the exclusion filter (AI-103).
12. **AI-112 — Feedback closes the loop.** Impressions, clicks, purchases, and dismissals on recommendations are logged against the serving request ID (AI-109), so the next ranking can learn from them and ai-evaluation can measure whether it did.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-051 — One static list under a "For you" label.** Banned: a "Recommended for you" rail that renders the same hard-coded or globally fixed list to every visitor regardless of history. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: compute the list from the user's events (AI-101, AI-107), or serve the fallback under its honest label (AI-105, AI-106). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-052 — Cosmetic exclusion filter.** Banned: exclusion that exists on paper but not in the serving path — purchased or out-of-stock items keep being recommended because filtering is a prompt hint, a UI-side hide, or code that never runs. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: remove owned, consumed, unavailable, and ineligible items in deterministic code after candidate generation, rechecked at serve time (AI-103, AI-104). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-053 — Fabricated recommendation reasons.** Banned: reason text that does not come from a signal that actually fired — template strings like "Because you loved X" attached to items the user never viewed, bought, or rated. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: generate the reason from the logged ranking signal for that item, and omit the reason when no signal fired (AI-110, AI-109). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-054 — Hidden hard-coded promotion.** Banned: a specific product or seller boosted inside a personalized rail by a hard-coded rule in code, with no entry in the serving config and no disclosure. Defeats: DET-FAKE-009. Instead: declare the boost as a named config entry, disclose it where the surface requires, and keep it behind the exclusion filter (AI-111, AI-108). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-AI-055 — Seed or demo items in a production rail.** Banned: recommendations drawn from seed, fixture, or demo catalog data presented to real users as purchasable products. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: generate candidates only from the live catalog, and keep demo data behind a visibly labeled demo mode (AI-102). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-051 — Two-user divergence test.** Verifies: AI-107, AI-101. Check (automated): seed two test users through the event API — user A with views and purchases of trail-running items, user B with views and purchases of baking items — then call the recommendations endpoint for each and compare the top-10 item ID lists. Pass: the two lists are not identical. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-052 — Exclusion sweep.** Verifies: AI-103, AI-104. Check (automated): for a test user, mark one item purchased and set one item out of stock, then request recommendations 20 times (or exhaust the candidate pool) and assert neither item ID appears in any response. Pass: zero appearances across all responses. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-053 — Cold-start fallback test.** Verifies: AI-105, AI-106. Check (automated): create a fresh user with no events, call the recommendations endpoint, and assert (a) the response is non-empty, (b) the items match the documented fallback configuration, and (c) the returned surface label is the fallback label, not "For you". Pass: all three assertions hold. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-054 — Serving-log completeness check.** Verifies: AI-109, AI-110, AI-112. Check (automated): make one recommendations request, then query the serving log by that request ID and assert the record carries model/config version, personalized-or-fallback flag, served item IDs, and a reason code per item. Pass: all fields present. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-055 — Boost and ranking config audit.** Verifies: AI-111, AI-108. Check (manual): serve recommendations to a neutral test user, list every item whose position is explained by a boost, and confirm each one has a named entry in the serving config and that the documented ranking logic matches the config. Pass: no undeclared boosts; document and config agree. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Events first: no event stream, no personalization claim.
- Filter in code, after candidates — never in a prompt.
- Fallback exists for every segment, and it wears its own label.
- "For you" is a promise: the list must differ by history.
- Log the version with every response, or quality is a rumor.

## Checklist

- [ ] Views, clicks, purchases, and dismissals are logged in the defined event schema from launch (AI-101).
- [ ] Serving runs candidates → exclusion filter → ranking → response, with no stage skipped (AI-102).
- [ ] Purchased, consumed, out-of-stock, and ineligible items never appear in any response; the exclusion sweep passes (AI-103, AI-104, G-AI-052).
- [ ] Two test users with different histories receive different lists (AI-107, G-AI-051).
- [ ] A cold-start user receives the documented fallback, non-empty and labeled as fallback — never "For you" (AI-105, AI-106, G-AI-053).
- [ ] Every response is logged with model/config version, fallback flag, item IDs, and reason codes; feedback events join on the request ID (AI-109, AI-112, G-AI-054).
- [ ] Each item's displayed reason comes from a signal that actually fired, and dismiss / "not interested" corrections change future output (AI-110).
- [ ] All boosts are named serving-config entries; no hard-coded promotion exists in code (AI-111, G-AI-055).

# search-relevance

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D17 AI Features (AI)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/custom-ranking ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/ranking
- **Depends on:** embeddings-search
- **Feeds into:** ai-evaluation, ai-observability

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** building or tuning a search feature whose results are ranked — candidate retrieval, ranking signals and weights, filters and sorting, zero-result handling — or when a ranking change, boost, or reranker is proposed.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is indexing and embedding the corpus (use embeddings-search), answering questions from retrieved documents (use rag-retrieval), or ranking a personalized recommendation feed (use recommendations). This skill owns the relevance of query-driven search results.

## Rules

1. **AI-121 — Ranking is tuned against a maintained judged query set.** The set holds real queries drawn from query logs, each with graded relevance labels for its expected results. It is versioned in the repo, and it — not opinion — is the baseline every tuning decision is measured against.
2. **AI-122 — No ranking change ships without an offline NDCG comparison.** Before release, the candidate ranking is scored against the current ranking on the judged set (AI-121) and NDCG@10 for both is recorded in the change. A regression blocks the release.
3. **AI-123 — The judged set grows from real query logs.** Each review cycle, zero-result queries and reformulated queries (the user immediately searched again in different words) are triaged: labeled and added to the set, or fixed and recorded as fixed.
4. **AI-124 — Zero-result rate is a monitored metric with a named owner.** Every zero-result search is logged with its query and active filters. The owner reviews the log on the recorded cycle and fixes causes — missing synonyms, unhandled spelling variants, indexing gaps — at the cause, not per complaint.
5. **AI-125 — Fixes target the query class, never one query.** A change must improve the class of queries that share the failure (a synonym group, a field-weight problem, an indexing gap). A boost, pin, or special case that helps exactly one query string is forbidden.
6. **AI-126 — A zero-result search returns an honest recovery state.** The state says that nothing matched, shows the active query and filters, and offers a working path: clear or loosen filters, corrected spelling, or the closest broader category. A blank area is never the answer.
7. **AI-127 — Filters never silently contradict the query.** Active filters are always visible, result counts are computed by the same query that produces the results, and when a filter combination excludes everything the query itself would match, the UI says so and offers to remove the conflicting filter.
8. **AI-128 — Paid and boosted placement is labeled and kept honest.** Sponsored or business-boosted results carry a visible label and are visually distinguishable from organic results. Payment never changes the organic ranking order while the surface presents that order as relevance.
9. **AI-129 — Sort labels say what the sort does.** The default order may be labeled "Relevance" only when it is produced by the ranking signals (AI-132). An order by date, price, or popularity is labeled by that field, never dressed up as relevance.
10. **AI-130 — Any LLM reranker carries a latency and cost budget.** The reranker runs under a recorded per-query latency budget and cost budget, with a timeout that falls back to the non-LLM ranking. A reranker with no budget or no fallback is forbidden.
11. **AI-131 — Search queries the real index over the real dataset.** Queries reach a server-side index over the full catalog or corpus; a record added through the product becomes findable without a redeploy. Filtering a small client-side array and presenting it as the catalog is forbidden.
12. **AI-132 — Ranking signals are explicit, weighted configuration.** The signals (semantic relevance, keyword match, freshness, popularity, document fields, business rules) and their weights live in one versioned ranking configuration. Scattered hard-coded boosts in feature code are forbidden.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AI-061 — Search with canned results.** Banned: every query returning the same fixture list, or results filtered client-side from a small hard-coded array presented as the catalog. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: query the server index over the real dataset so contents and counts vary with the query and the data (AI-131). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-062 — Sort and filter controls that only rearrange a fixture.** Banned: sort, filter, and pagination controls that reorder one small hard-coded set while counts and pages claim a larger dataset. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: execute filtering, sorting, and pagination against the real dataset with counts derived from the same query (AI-127, AI-131). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AI-063 — Blank zero-result state.** Banned: a search that matches nothing renders an empty container with no explanation. Defeats: DET-UX-009. Instead: render the recovery state — what matched nothing, the active constraints, and the next action (AI-126). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-AI-064 — Filter dead end with invisible constraints.** Banned: a filter combination returning zero results while the active filters are hidden and no clear-or-adjust action exists. Defeats: DET-UX-025. Instead: show active filters on the results view and offer one-action clear/broaden whenever results are empty (AI-126, AI-127). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-AI-065 — Paid placement disguised as relevance.** Banned: sponsored or boosted items inserted into the organic order, unlabeled, so payment reads as relevance. Defeats: DET-FAKE-017. Instead: label boosted placement visibly, keep it distinguishable from the organic order, and record every boost in the ranking configuration (AI-128, AI-132). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AI-061 — Offline NDCG regression gate.** Verifies: AI-121, AI-122. Check (automated): run the project's eval script, e.g. `python3 scripts/search_eval.py --judged search/judged-queries.json --candidate candidate --baseline current`, which prints NDCG@10 for both rankings. Pass: candidate NDCG@10 is at or above the baseline, and both scores are recorded in the change. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-062 — Zero-result audit.** Verifies: AI-123, AI-124. Check (automated): run the zero-result report over the period's query log, e.g. `python3 scripts/zero_result_report.py --log search-queries.log`, which prints the zero-result rate and the untriaged zero-result queries. Pass: the rate is at or below the recorded threshold and every listed query is either added to the judged set with labels or recorded as fixed with its cause. Fail: block shipment of the ranking release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-063 — Findability and honesty probe.** Verifies: AI-131. Check (automated): create a record containing a unique marker term through the product's normal write path, search the marker, then search a gibberish string. Pass: the marker search returns the new record with no redeploy, and the gibberish search returns the honest zero-result state (AI-126). Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-064 — Filter recovery walk.** Verifies: AI-126, AI-127. Check (manual): in the running product, run a nonsense search, then apply a filter combination that excludes everything the query matches. Pass: both cases show what matched nothing, display the active query and filters, and offer a working clear/broaden action; counts shown equal the results the same query returns. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AI-065 — Placement and label audit.** Verifies: AI-128, AI-129, AI-132. Check (automated + manual): diff the ranking configuration for the release — every boost or pin must appear there with a reason — then inspect the rendered results for a boosted query. Pass: no boost exists outside the configuration, every boosted item carries its label in the UI, and the default sort is labeled "Relevance" only when produced by the configured signals. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No judged set, no tuning — opinion is not a baseline.
- Every ranking change records its NDCG delta.
- Zero results are logged, owned, and fixed at the cause.
- Fix the query class, never the one query.
- Boosted is labeled, or it does not ship.

## Checklist

- [ ] The judged query set is versioned, built from real queries with graded labels, and grew this cycle from zero-result and reformulated queries (AI-121, AI-123).
- [ ] The release records candidate vs. baseline NDCG@10 and shows no regression (AI-122, G-AI-061).
- [ ] The zero-result rate is reported, at or below threshold, with an owner and every untriaged query resolved (AI-124, G-AI-062).
- [ ] A newly created record is findable by search without a redeploy, and gibberish returns the honest empty state (AI-131, G-AI-063).
- [ ] Zero-result and impossible-filter states explain themselves, show active constraints, and offer a working recovery action (AI-126, AI-127, G-AI-064).
- [ ] All boosts live in the ranking configuration with reasons; boosted items are labeled in the UI; sort labels name the actual sort (AI-128, AI-129, AI-132, G-AI-065).
- [ ] Any LLM reranker has a recorded latency and cost budget and a tested timeout fallback to the non-LLM ranking (AI-130).
